qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Pure commodity price-taker. Upstream hydrocarbon production is sold at prevailing international market prices, while downstream refining profits are dictated by European crack spreads. Multi-cycle ROIC fails the 12% threshold due to severe cyclicality and non-recoverable impairment cycles.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Spanish integrated energy company with leading Iberian refining and retail distribution. Despite high-complexity refining assets and growing low-carbon power investments, Repsol is a structural commodity price-taker lacking pricing power above inflation. Financial performance is tethered to cyclical global crude benchmarks, Henry Hub gas prices, and volatile refining margins, compounded by Spanish government windfall energy taxes.
qualitative.evidence: Repsol operates across Upstream (crude and gas extraction in North America, Latin America, and North Africa), Industrial (5 refineries in Spain with ~1.0 mbpd capacity, large petrochemical complexes, and trading), and Commercial/Customer (retail marketing, mobility, and low-carbon electricity/gas generation). Multi-cycle ROIC is deeply cyclical and fails the 12% Munger bar across a full 10-year cycle: 10-year average ROIC is ~6-7%, characterized by massive write-downs during cyclical downturns (e.g., €3.8B impairment in 2019 anticipating decarbonization, and deep losses in 2020 with negative net income of -€3.29B). In 2022-2023, while refining margins surged temporarily, profits were heavily dampened by Spain's 1.2% windfall tax on energy revenue. Repsol possesses zero ability to raise fuel or chemical prices independently of spot market dynamics.
